words.register: Informal but socially acceptable in common settings.
misconceptions: mistaken for slang because it is informal

words.connotation: Edgy, intimate, potentially exclusionary, often cool.
words.register: Very informal, restricted to specific contexts or groups.
misconceptions: mistaken for colloquial because it is spoken

semantic_axes.description: How universally accepted the term is (accepted by broad society vs. restricted to a subculture).
Likelihood of lasting in the language (well-established vs. quickly changing).
Whether the term includes broad speakers or functions as a marker for a specific group identity.

colloquial: She told me, 'I'm kinda tired,' as she sat down.
It's a colloquial way of saying hello.
They just had a chat about the weekend.
He's a nice guy, very easy to talk to.
Give me a sec; I'll be right back.
slang: The gamers called the new player a noob.
She's totally ghosting him, which is so mean.
That outfit is lit, everyone was talking about it.
I'm feeling kind of sus about this whole situation.
Don't be salty just because you lost.
That's just internet slang that will fade away.

colloquial: The skaters called the trick a 'kickflip' (slang is better here).
They used a lot of weird internet slang in their presentation.
He kept calling everyone 'fam' in a weird way.
That new term is total subculture slang.
She was trying to use cool slang and looked silly.
They made up their own secret code.
slang: It was a relaxed, standard way of speaking to a friend.
The professor used a conversational tone for the lecture.
He was just being a bit informal, not using any jargon.
Their everyday speech was perfectly standard.
They were chatting in a natural, friendly manner.
It was just a casual remark, not jargon.

edges.boundary_rule: Use colloquial for casual, standard, everyday speech; use slang for non-standard, restricted, group-specific, or ephemeral terms.

misconceptions.M3: Assuming slang is just a synonym for bad grammar.

chains.frame: How Marcus describes his meeting with his brother: ___

beats.text: Marcus told me, 'Yeah, we just hung out and watched TV.'
beats.reason: It's standard conversational English, not niche.

beats.text: Marcus added, 'I mean, it wasn't super formal, just comfy.'

chains.feedback_short: It's standard conversational language. 'Hung out' and 'comfy' are common, standard, informal, not restricted to any group.
chains.feedback_deep: Even though it's informal, it's widely used and perfectly understood across all standard English speakers. Slang is restricted, niche, or subcultural, which this is not.
chains.contrast_rule: Colloquial is for everyone's casual conversation; slang is for specific groups.
